title: Remote directory picker in the directory prompt and the Remotes pane
body:
Add a remote directory picker to the places that ask for a directory on a Remote, so the user can browse the Remote's folders instead of typing a path blind. Today src/remote_dir_prompt.rs (DirPrompt, the "Open a shell on <remote>" prompt with one Directory text field) and the per-Project directory rows in the Remotes pane edit form (src/remotes_pane.rs, Field::Dir) take typed text only.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md (sections: Launch > Directory, UI > Launcher, UI > Settings > Remotes). Add a short part describing what you build. Feature doc: docs/remote-sessions.md (gotchas only).
Blocked by: Install a missing agent CLI on a Remote from the UI
Decided, do not reopen:
- It is a directory picker only (a Session starts in a directory). Files are not listed.
- It is an inline list under the Directory field, not a separate window or tree: the text field stays the source of truth, and the list shows the sub-directories of the directory the field currently names (the part up to the last separator; what follows it filters the list by prefix). Choosing an entry writes it into the field and lists the next level; a ".." entry goes up; "~" is the home directory and stays written as "~/..." when under home. Typing still works exactly as today with no listing needed, and Enter on the field still accepts whatever is typed.
- Listing runs over ssh with BatchMode (as Test does in src/remote_probe.rs), off the UI thread, with a deadline, debounced while typing, and cached per (target, directory) for the life of the prompt. Never on the frame path. A Remote that needs a password prompt cannot be listed: say so plainly in the list area and leave typing working.
- The remote command is built with the existing quoting in src/remote.rs (sh_quote / ps_quote and the base64 line forms posix_line / utf16le_b64); the typed path is data and must never be interpolated into a shell line unquoted. Posix: list directory entries only, dot-directories included but sorted after the others, cap the count (say 500) and say when it was cut. Pwsh / WindowsPowerShell: the equivalent with Get-ChildItem -Directory -Force, including listing drive roots when the field is empty or a bare drive is needed; label this path untested (no Windows Remote exists) in the spec and feature doc.
- Foreman copies nothing to the Remote and installs nothing there.
Do:
1. A pure model (new module, for example src/remote_browse.rs): split the field text into (directory to list, filter prefix) for Posix and Windows path styles, join a chosen entry back into the field text, go up one level, keep "~" forms, and parse the listing output (names with spaces, quotes, non-ASCII, a trailing newline, an empty directory, a permission-denied or no-such-directory error turned into a plain message). Table tests for all of it.
2. The probe: one function that returns a cached state for (target, shell, directory): Loading, Listed(entries, truncated), or Failed(plain message), starting the ssh off-thread on first ask, exactly the shape remote_probe::reach uses. Unit-test the argv it would run without spawning ssh.
3. remote_dir_prompt: under the Directory field, a list area with a FIXED reserved height (nothing shifts when a listing arrives), a vertical scroll, and one row per directory. Keyboard: Down from the field enters the list, Up/Down move, Right or Enter on a row descends into it (writes it to the field), Left or Backspace on an empty filter goes up, Tab or Up from the first row returns to the field, Esc still cancels the prompt, and Enter in the FIELD still opens. Mouse: click a row to descend, the existing open/cancel buttons unchanged. Show Loading and Failed in words inside the list area, and the directory being listed as a one-line breadcrumb that elides from the front. The hint line must tell the truth for both states (field focused, list focused) and fit on one line.
4. Remotes pane edit form: the same list for the focused Field::Dir row, shown in a reserved area of the form so the rows do not jump, reusing the same widget and model. Ctrl+Backspace (forget) and the existing hints keep working; every hint still fits one line at PANE_MIN_W.
Design bar (a designer reviews this from the code afterwards; earlier cards failed on these): theme tokens only, no hard-coded colours or sizes where siblings use theme values; every state readable without colour alone (loading, empty directory, failed, truncated, selected row, hovered row); long names truncate with the full name on hover; nothing shifts when a result arrives; the prompt does not grow taller than a small window can show (the list scrolls, the buttons stay visible); the selected row and the text field cannot both look focused at once; Enter never does two things (descend vs open) in the same state.
The test Remote is andy@100.102.251.37 (Debian, key login, never ask for a password). You may run read-only directory listings against it to check the Posix command by hand; do not write, create or delete anything there.
Done when:
- table tests for the path model and the listing parser; a test on the ssh argv; the cache never starts a second listing for the same key while one is running
- egui::Context::run tests: the list area height is the same in Loading, Listed, empty and Failed; Down/Right/Left/Enter behave as specified and Enter in the field opens; at PANE_MIN_W and at the dir prompt's width every row and both hints stay inside their rects
- the launcher model and the directory prompt with a Remote that cannot be listed behave as today (typing works, Enter opens)
- the full test suite passes
- the final report lists the states the human should capture with build-screenshot, and says what was run against the test Remote
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent
